question.problem:
Written in **ascending order**, the solutions to $|2-k|=9$ are $k=${{field-1}} and $k=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|2-k|=2-k,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2-k| & =9 \\ 2-k & =9 \\ -k & =7 \\ k & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|2-k|=-(2-k),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2-k| & =9 \\ -(2-k) & =9 \\ -2+k & =9 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $k=-7$ and $k=11.$
